title: LFO: movement
learned: Control voltage (CV) turns a knob for you; an LFO turns it back and forth
The CV amount knob next to an input sets how far the CV moves
RATE: slow is a sweep, fast a wobble; very fast becomes a sound of its own
LFO on the filter = movement in colour, on FM = vibrato

steps.why: A sound that never changes gets boring fast. You could keep turning a knob by hand, or let a voltage do it. A low-frequency oscillator (LFO) is an oscillator too slow to hear: it makes a voltage that rises and falls by itself.
steps.do: The pluck from the last lesson plays. An LFO (JX-LFO) is in the rack. Press Next.

steps.why: First let the LFO move the filter cutoff.
steps.do: Drag a cable from TRI of the LFO to FREQ CV of the filter.
steps.after: No change yet: the FREQ CV knob of the filter is in the middle, so the voltage moves nothing.

steps.why: FREQ CV on the front is the amount knob for that input.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn FREQ CV of the filter (MODULATION row) to the right.
steps.after: The notes now get brighter and darker in a slow wave: the LFO turns CUTOFF for you. Its triangle goes from -5 V to +5 V; at full FREQ CV that is five octaves up and five down.

steps.why: RATE sets how fast the LFO goes.
steps.do: Turn RATE of the LFO up and down.
steps.after: Slow, it is a sweep over many notes. Fast, it becomes a wobble. Near the top of the knob the LFO runs hundreds of times a second: that is no longer movement but a new sound, because CV and audio are the same thing at different speeds.

steps.why: Now the pitch. The oscillator's FM input moves its pitch, scaled by its FM knob.
steps.do: Press F2 and drag a cable from SIN of the LFO to FM of the oscillator.
steps.after: No change yet: the FM knob of the oscillator is in the middle.

steps.why: Pitch is sensitive: a little goes a long way.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn FM of the oscillator just a little to the right.
steps.after: The pitch now wavers gently: vibrato, like a singer. Turn FM further and it becomes a siren: at 10 % the LFO's ±5 V moves the pitch half an octave up and down.
steps.try: Turn RATE of the LFO: a slow vibrato sounds lazy, a fast one nervous. About 5 per second sounds most natural.

steps.do: An LFO is a hand that turns knobs for you. Press Next to finish.
